questions.title: Create a Deployment
questions.text:
Create a new namespace named `frontend`.

In that namespace, create a Deployment named `web` with image `nginx:1.27`, exposing container port `80`, running `3` replicas.

All replicas should be running when you are done.

checks.name: frontend
checks.hint: namespace frontend does not exist

checks.name: web
checks.hint: deployment web in frontend must have 3 replicas, image nginx:1.27 and container port 80

checks.name: web
checks.hint: not all replicas of web are available

questions.solution:
Imperative commands are fastest here:

    kubectl create namespace frontend
    kubectl create deployment web --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=3 --port=80 -n frontend
    kubectl -n frontend rollout status deployment web

`--port` adds the containerPort to the pod template. That is the whole task.

**Alternative, if you prefer to work from YAML** (a habit that pays off on harder questions): generate the manifest with `$do` (`--dry-run=client -o yaml`), review or edit it, then apply it. The file only exists after the first command writes it:

    kubectl create deployment web --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=3 --port=80 -n frontend $do > web.yaml
    vim web.yaml
    kubectl apply -f web.yaml

questions.title: Scale a Deployment
questions.text:
The Deployment `api` in namespace `backend` currently runs 2 replicas.

Scale it to `5` replicas.

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api should have 5 available replicas

questions.solution:
kubectl scale deployment api -n backend --replicas=5
    kubectl -n backend get deployment api

Scaling only changes `spec.replicas`; the ReplicaSet controller creates the extra pods. `kubectl edit deployment api -n backend` and changing `replicas` works too.

questions.title: Multi-container Pod
questions.text:
Create a Pod named `multi` in namespace `default` with two containers:

- a container named `web` using image `nginx:1.27`
- a container named `sidecar` using image `busybox:1.36` running the command `sleep 3600`

Both containers must be running.

checks.name: multi
checks.hint: pod multi must have exactly two containers

checks.name: multi
checks.hint: container web with image nginx:1.27 is missing

checks.name: multi
checks.hint: container sidecar with image busybox:1.36 is missing

checks.name: multi
checks.hint: pod multi is not running with all containers ready

questions.solution:
Generate a skeleton, then add the second container in vim:

    kubectl run multi --image=nginx:1.27 $do > multi.yaml
    vim multi.yaml

Make the containers list look like this (the first container is renamed to `web`):

    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.27
      - name: sidecar
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep", "3600"]

Then `kubectl apply -f multi.yaml` and confirm `2/2` in `kubectl get pod multi`.

references.title: Define a command for a container

questions.title: Schedule with a node selector
questions.text:
One of the worker nodes carries the label `disk=ssd`.

Create a Pod named `ssd-pod` in namespace `default` with image `nginx:1.27` that is scheduled **only** onto a node with that label, using a node selector. The Pod must be running.

checks.name: ssd-pod
checks.hint: ssd-pod must use nodeSelector disk=ssd and image nginx:1.27

checks.name: ssd-pod
checks.hint: ssd-pod is not running on the disk=ssd node

questions.solution:
Find the node first, then place the pod with `nodeSelector`:

    kubectl get nodes -l disk=ssd
    kubectl run ssd-pod --image=nginx:1.27 $do > ssd-pod.yaml
    vim ssd-pod.yaml      # add under spec:
    #   nodeSelector:
    #     disk: ssd
    kubectl apply -f ssd-pod.yaml
    kubectl get pod ssd-pod -o wide

`nodeSelector` is the simplest form of node affinity: the scheduler only considers nodes whose labels include every key/value listed.

questions.title: Taints and tolerations
questions.text:
Taint node `cka-node2` with key `env`, value `prod` and effect `NoSchedule`.

Then create a Pod named `prod-pod` in namespace `default` with image `nginx:1.27` that tolerates this taint and runs on `cka-node2`. (Use a node selector or `nodeName` to place it there.)

checks.hint: node cka-node2 must carry taint env=prod:NoSchedule

checks.name: prod-pod
checks.hint: prod-pod needs a toleration for key env with effect NoSchedule

checks.name: prod-pod
checks.hint: prod-pod is not running on cka-node2

questions.solution:
kubectl taint nodes cka-node2 env=prod:NoSchedule
    kubectl describe node cka-node2 | grep -A2 Taints

Then a pod that tolerates the taint and is pinned to the node:

    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: prod-pod
    spec:
      nodeName: cka-node2
      tolerations:
      - key: env
        operator: Equal
        value: prod
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27

A toleration only *allows* scheduling onto the tainted node; it does not force it. `nodeName` (or a `nodeSelector` on `kubernetes.io/hostname: cka-node2`) is what pins the pod. Remove a taint later with a trailing dash: `kubectl taint nodes cka-node2 env=prod:NoSchedule-`.

questions.title: Expose a Deployment
questions.text:
Expose the Deployment `api` in namespace `backend` with a Service named `api-svc` of type `ClusterIP`.

The Service must listen on port `8080` and forward to the container port `80`.

Verify that the Service has endpoints.

checks.name: api-svc
checks.hint: api-svc must be ClusterIP, port 8080 -> targetPort 80, selecting app=api

checks.name: api-svc
checks.hint: api-svc has no endpoints

questions.solution:
kubectl expose deployment api -n backend --name=api-svc --port=8080 --target-port=80 --type=ClusterIP
    kubectl -n backend get endpoints api-svc

`expose` copies the Deployment's selector (`app=api`) into the Service. Endpoints only appear for pods that match the selector **and** are Ready — an empty ENDPOINTS column almost always means a selector/label mismatch.

questions.title: NetworkPolicy
questions.text:
In namespace `db` there is a Deployment `db` (pods labelled `app=db`) listening on TCP port `6379`.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `allow-api-to-db` in namespace `db` so that pods labelled `app=db` accept **ingress** traffic on TCP port `6379` **only** from pods in the same namespace labelled `role=api`. All other ingress to those pods must be denied.

You can verify with `kubectl exec api-client -n db -- nc -zv db 6379` style checks (the pods `api-client` and `intruder` exist for testing).

checks.name: allow-api-to-db
checks.hint: allow-api-to-db must select app=db and be an Ingress policy
pods with role=api must be able to reach app=db on 6379
pods without role=api must be blocked from app=db

questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: allow-api-to-db
      namespace: db
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: db
      policyTypes:
      - Ingress
      ingress:
      - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              role: api
        ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 6379

Once any policy selects a pod for Ingress, everything not explicitly allowed is denied — that is what makes `intruder` fail. Verify from both test pods:

    kubectl -n db exec api-client -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 db:6379   # works
    kubectl -n db exec intruder   -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 db:6379   # times out

questions.title: PersistentVolume and claim
questions.text:
Create a PersistentVolume named `pv-data` with:

- capacity `1Gi`
- access mode `ReadWriteOnce`
- `hostPath` at `/mnt/data`
- `storageClassName: manual`

Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `pvc-data` in namespace `default` requesting `500Mi` with access mode `ReadWriteOnce` and `storageClassName: manual`, so that it binds to `pv-data`.

Finally create a Pod named `data-pod` in namespace `default` with image `nginx:1.27` that mounts the claim at `/usr/share/nginx/html`.

checks.name: pv-data
checks.hint: pv-data must be 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /mnt/data, storageClassName manual

checks.name: pvc-data
checks.hint: pvc-data must be Bound to pv-data

checks.name: data-pod
checks.hint: data-pod must mount pvc-data at /usr/share/nginx/html

checks.name: data-pod
checks.hint: data-pod is not running

questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolume
    metadata:
      name: pv-data
    spec:
      capacity:
        storage: 1Gi
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      storageClassName: manual
      hostPath:
        path: /mnt/data
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      name: pvc-data
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      storageClassName: manual
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 500Mi
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: data-pod
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: pvc-data
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html

Put all three in one file and `kubectl apply -f`. A claim binds to a volume whose storageClassName matches, whose access modes include the requested ones, and whose capacity is at least the request — check with `kubectl get pv,pvc`.

references.title: Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume

questions.title: StorageClass
questions.text:
Create a StorageClass named `fast-local` with:

- provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`
- `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`
- `reclaimPolicy: Delete`

checks.name: fast-local
checks.hint: fast-local must use rancher.io/local-path, WaitForFirstConsumer and Delete

questions.solution:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
    kind: StorageClass
    metadata:
      name: fast-local
    provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
    volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
    reclaimPolicy: Delete

Note that `provisioner`, `reclaimPolicy` and `volumeBindingMode` are top-level fields on a StorageClass, not under `spec`. `WaitForFirstConsumer` delays volume creation until a pod using the claim is scheduled, so the volume lands on the right node.

questions.title: RBAC for a ServiceAccount
questions.text:
In namespace `apps`:

- create a ServiceAccount named `deploy-bot`
- create a Role named `deploy-manager` that allows the verbs `create`, `get`, `list` and `update` on `deployments`
- create a RoleBinding named `deploy-bot-binding` that binds the Role to the ServiceAccount

The ServiceAccount must **not** be able to delete deployments or create pods.

checks.name: deploy-bot
checks.hint: serviceaccount deploy-bot missing in apps

checks.name: deploy-manager
checks.hint: role deploy-manager missing in apps

checks.name: deploy-bot-binding
checks.hint: rolebinding deploy-bot-binding missing in apps
deploy-bot cannot create deployments in apps
deploy-bot cannot list deployments in apps
deploy-bot must not be able to delete deployments
deploy-bot must not be able to create pods

questions.solution:
kubectl -n apps create serviceaccount deploy-bot
    kubectl -n apps create role deploy-manager --verb=create,get,list,update --resource=deployments
    kubectl -n apps create rolebinding deploy-bot-binding --role=deploy-manager --serviceaccount=apps:deploy-bot

Verify with impersonation:

    kubectl -n apps auth can-i create deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:apps:deploy-bot   # yes
    kubectl -n apps auth can-i delete deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:apps:deploy-bot   # no

A Role is namespaced and grants nothing by itself; the RoleBinding attaches it to a subject. ServiceAccount subjects are written `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name>`.

questions.title: etcd backup
questions.text:
Create a snapshot of the etcd instance running on the control plane node `cka-control` and save it to `/opt/etcd-backup.db` on that node.

The following TLS material is available under `/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/`:

- CA certificate: `ca.crt`
- client certificate: `server.crt`
- client key: `server.key`

The etcd endpoint is `https://127.0.0.1:2379`.

checks.hint: /opt/etcd-backup.db does not exist on cka-control or is not an etcd snapshot

questions.solution:
ssh cka-control
    sudo -i
    ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /opt/etcd-backup.db \
      --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
      --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
      --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
      --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key
    ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /opt/etcd-backup.db -w table

Root is needed because the key files are mode 600. Without the three TLS flags etcdctl cannot authenticate and fails with `context deadline exceeded`. The certificate paths can always be read from the etcd static pod manifest: `cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml | grep -E 'cert|key|trusted'`.

references.title: Operating etcd clusters — Backing up an etcd cluster

questions.title: Upgrade the control plane
questions.text:
The cluster `k8s-ops` runs Kubernetes `1.31.0`. Upgrade **only the control plane node** `ops-control` to version `1.31.2`:

- upgrade `kubeadm`, run the upgrade, then upgrade `kubelet` and `kubectl`
- drain the node before upgrading and make it schedulable again afterwards
- the packages are held with `apt-mark`; version strings look like `1.31.2-1.1`

When you are done, `kubectl get nodes` must show `ops-control` at `v1.31.2` and `Ready`.

checks.hint: the control plane (kubeadm upgrade apply) is not at v1.31.2
kubelet on ops-control is not reporting v1.31.2 (upgrade the kubelet package and restart it)
ops-control is still cordoned
ops-control is not Ready

questions.solution:
From the base host, drain the node, then do the package work on the node itself:

    kubectl config use-context k8s-ops
    kubectl drain ops-control --ignore-daemonsets
    ssh ops-control
    sudo -i
    apt-mark unhold kubeadm && apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.31.2-1.1 && apt-mark hold kubeadm
    kubeadm version
    kubeadm upgrade plan
    kubeadm upgrade apply v1.31.2
    apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && apt-get install -y kubelet=1.31.2-1.1 kubectl=1.31.2-1.1 && apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl restart kubelet
    exit
    exit
    kubectl uncordon ops-control
    kubectl get nodes

Order matters: kubeadm first (it drives the control-plane upgrade), then `kubeadm upgrade apply`, then kubelet/kubectl. The node reports its version from the running kubelet, so it only shows v1.31.2 after the restart. Worker nodes use `kubeadm upgrade node` instead of `apply`.

questions.title: Node NotReady
questions.text:
The worker node `ops-node2` in cluster `k8s-ops` is in `NotReady` state.

Investigate and fix the problem so that the node becomes `Ready`. Make sure the fix is permanent (the responsible service must be enabled).

checks.name: kubelet
checks.hint: kubelet on ops-node2 is not active and enabled
ops-node2 is still NotReady

questions.solution:
kubectl get nodes
    kubectl describe node ops-node2       # Ready condition: Unknown, "Kubelet stopped posting node status"
    ssh ops-node2
    systemctl status kubelet              # inactive (dead)
    sudo systemctl enable --now kubelet   # start it and make it survive reboots
    systemctl status kubelet
    exit
    kubectl get nodes                     # Ready

A NotReady node nearly always means the kubelet is down or cannot reach the API server. Check `systemctl status kubelet` first, then `journalctl -u kubelet` for why it failed (bad config path, wrong certificates, swap enabled, container runtime down).

questions.title: Broken Deployment
questions.text:
The Deployment `checkout` in namespace `shop` has pods that are not running.

Find the cause and fix the Deployment in place (do not delete and recreate it). The intended image is `nginx:1.27-alpine`. All replicas must become available.

checks.name: checkout
checks.hint: checkout must use image nginx:1.27-alpine

checks.name: checkout
checks.hint: not all replicas of checkout are available

questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop get pods                                  # ImagePullBackOff
    kubectl -n shop describe pod <checkout-pod> | tail -n 15  # "failed to pull image nginx:1.27-alpne"
    kubectl -n shop set image deployment/checkout nginx=nginx:1.27-alpine
    kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment checkout

`set image` (or `kubectl edit deployment checkout`) changes the pod template, which triggers a new ReplicaSet — the deployment itself is never deleted. `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff` are almost always a typo in the image name or tag; `describe pod` shows the exact string the kubelet tried to pull.

questions.title: Find the busiest Pod
questions.text:
Using the metrics available in the cluster, find the Pod in namespace `monitoring` that consumes the **most CPU**.

Write only the Pod's name into the file `/opt/answers/high-cpu.txt` on the base host (the host you are logged into when the exam starts).

checks.hint: /opt/answers/high-cpu.txt on cka-base must contain exactly the name of the highest-CPU pod in monitoring

questions.solution:
kubectl top pods -n monitoring --sort-by=cpu
    echo log-shipper > /opt/answers/high-cpu.txt
    cat /opt/answers/high-cpu.txt

`kubectl top` reads the Metrics API (served by metrics-server); `--sort-by=cpu` or `--sort-by=memory` puts the biggest consumer first. Write the name only, with no extra text, when a question asks for an answer file.

questions.title: Service without endpoints
questions.text:
In namespace `shop`, the Service `orders-svc` is supposed to route traffic to the pods of the Deployment `orders`, but it has no endpoints.

Fix the Service so that it selects the `orders` pods. Do not change the Deployment.

checks.name: orders-svc
checks.hint: orders-svc selector must match the orders pods (app=orders)

checks.name: orders-svc
checks.hint: orders-svc still has no endpoints

checks.name: orders
checks.hint: the orders Deployment must not be changed

questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop get endpoints orders-svc                 # <none>
    kubectl -n shop get svc orders-svc -o wide               # SELECTOR app=order
    kubectl -n shop get pods --show-labels                   # pods carry app=orders
    kubectl -n shop patch svc orders-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"orders"}}}'
    kubectl -n shop get endpoints orders-svc                 # two pod IPs

`kubectl edit svc orders-svc -n shop` works just as well. The Service selector must match the pod labels exactly; comparing `get svc -o wide` with `get pods --show-labels` finds these in seconds.

questions.title: DaemonSet on every node
questions.text:
Create a DaemonSet named `log-agent` in namespace `kube-system` using image `busybox:1.36` with the command `sleep 3600`.

It must run one Pod on **every** node of the cluster, including the control plane node.

checks.name: log-agent
checks.hint: daemonset log-agent with image busybox:1.36 missing in kube-system

checks.name: log-agent
checks.hint: log-agent does not have a running pod on every node (control plane taint?)

questions.solution:
There is no `kubectl create daemonset`; the quickest route is to generate a Deployment and edit it:

    kubectl -n kube-system create deployment log-agent --image=busybox:1.36 $do -- sleep 3600 > ds.yaml
    vim ds.yaml     # kind: DaemonSet, delete replicas and strategy, add the toleration

    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: DaemonSet
    metadata:
      name: log-agent
      namespace: kube-system
    spec:
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: log-agent
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: log-agent
        spec:
          tolerations:
          - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
            operator: Exists
            effect: NoSchedule
          containers:
          - name: agent
            image: busybox:1.36
            command: ["sleep", "3600"]

Control-plane nodes carry a `NoSchedule` taint, so without the toleration the DaemonSet skips them. `kubectl -n kube-system get ds log-agent` should show DESIRED equal to the node count.

questions.title: Ingress
questions.text:
In namespace `www` there is a Deployment `www` exposed by the Service `www` on port `80`.

Create an Ingress named `www-ingress` in namespace `www` that routes requests for host `www.example.com` and path `/` (pathType `Prefix`) to Service `www` on port `80`. Use the ingress class `nginx`.

checks.name: www-ingress
checks.hint: www-ingress must route www.example.com / (Prefix) to service www:80 with ingressClassName nginx

questions.solution:
kubectl -n www create ingress www-ingress --class=nginx --rule="www.example.com/*=www:80"
    kubectl -n www get ingress www-ingress -o yaml

The `/*` in the rule produces `pathType: Prefix` (a plain `/` gives `Exact`). Equivalent YAML:

    apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Ingress
    metadata:
      name: www-ingress
      namespace: www
    spec:
      ingressClassName: nginx
      rules:
      - host: www.example.com
        http:
          paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: www
                port:
                  number: 80
